newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin keen to cut spending, buy Russian - Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin keen to cut spending, buy Russian - Nemtsov.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is determined to cut government spending and will ensure that the state will not fund the purchase of foreign cars, new First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov told a news conference.

Nemtsov, speaking at a joint news conference with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and fellow first deputy premier Anatoly Chubais, said Yeltsin had promised to sign in three days a draft decree fighting corruption and boosting competition.
Foodstuffs for state reserves, as well as food and arms for the armed forces, would be tendered on a competitive basis as would state orders including road works.
There would be no more foreign cars at state expense for state officials, Nemtsov added. Foreign cars currently used by government officials would be auctioned off gradually.
The new minister was previous governor of the Nizhny Novgorod, where Russia's Volga cars are produced. He has already said his official car should be a Volga.
